classification.difficultyReason: Read an inverse prediction from a supplied line of best fit and explain the limitation of distant extrapolation.

content.prompt: The scatter graph shows the cost of rent per month for office space and the distance from the city centre.

spec.description: Fine square grid, arrowheaded axes, eight purple crosses and a red decreasing supplied line of best fit. The axis currency is corrected to dollars to agree with part b. Coordinates are visual estimates because the source provides no dataset.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal axis: distance from city centre, 0–50 km, labels every 5 km and grid every 1 km. Vertical axis: monthly rent, 0–2000 dollars, labels every 200 and grid every 40. Crosses approximately at (2.5,1600), (10,1400), (15,1400), (20,1320), (25,1200), (30,1000), (35,1200), (45,800). Supplied best-fit line approximately joins (2,1680) and (45,900).
spec.answerVisibility: All points and the best-fit line are permanent student-visible givens; no prediction guides or answers appear.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the direction of correlation shown in the scatter graph?

answer.worked: Negative correlation: rent generally decreases as distance from the city centre increases.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Estimate the distance from the city centre for an office space that costs $\$1000$ per month.

answer.worked: Read horizontally from a rent of $\$1000$ to the line of best fit, then vertically down to the distance axis. The distance is approximately 38 km; readings around 38–40 km are reasonable.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If the graph was extended up to 100 km from the city centre, do you think the trend shown by the line of best fit would continue? Explain your answer.

answer.short: No. This is far outside the existing data range, so the trend may change.
answer.worked: No. Predicting rent at 100 km would extrapolate far beyond the observed distances. The relationship may change, and continuing this decreasing line would eventually predict a negative rent.
